mission: BOUNDED CLOSURE REMEDIATION V1 - CHF quantitative cap must block child descent

scenario.source: The Borrower shall not make Restricted Payments in an aggregate amount exceeding CHF 2,000,000 in any fiscal year other than (a) intercompany dividends (b) tax distributions.
segmentation: ...exceeding CHF 2,000,000 in any fiscal year other than
scenario.inventorySpans: two CRITICAL items on the children only

before.childDescentDecision: granted - 'introduces an enumerated list whose 2 child clause(s) are each accounted for; carries no independent conjunct and no quantitative value of its own'

causalDifferential.conclusion: Segmentation, spans and the descent rule are byte-identical between the two. The only difference is whether the scanner returns a MONEY value, which is what the descent value guard consults. Replacing '$' with 'CHF ' flips the safety result. Root cause confirmed at the quantitative layer; child descent is not the defect and was not changed.

scannerChange.what: one additional MONEY PatternDef: /\b[A-Z]{3}\s?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?(?:\s?(?:million|billion|thousand|mm|bn))?\b/ (case-sensitive), normalize -> value via the existing parseMoney, unit = the captured three-letter code
scannerChange.architecture: generalises the shape the existing symbol pattern already carried for exactly one hardcoded code (USD\s?); the currency code lands in the existing `unit` field exactly as USD/GBP/EUR do - no schema change, no currency list, no FX, no normalisation across currencies
scannerChange.precedence: placed LAST in PATTERNS so every more specific unit shape claims its span first ('LTV 65%' stays PERCENT); the pre-existing symbol/USD pattern keeps first claim ('USD 2,000,000' still unit USD via the original path)
scannerChange.chfLiteralInProduction: appears only in the explanatory comment, never in code

falseMatchSafety.uppercaseTokenNoAmount: 'the ABC Facility and the LTV Covenant' -> []
falseMatchSafety.disclosedResidualFalsePositive: an uppercase three-letter token directly followed by a bare number that no other unit explains (e.g. 'LTV 65' with no %) is now MONEY with unit 'LTV'. This errs in the conservative direction - a value surfaces for review rather than vanishes - and is disclosed rather than hidden.
